ranking.rationale: Exact match: the Wish is a mechanical cast-shadow theatre using an ordinary external light, one rotating control, exact occluders, and three inspectable projected stories. Orin's Taste explicitly requires light direction, projection plane, distance band, state angles, alignment cue, and honest unverified optics.

Strong alternate for hand-powered shadow, aperture, and rotating-mask work with few broad parts, but its broader optical-transformation craft is less specifically centred on a projected second story than Orin's mechanical shadow theatre.

The large wheel, indexing, full motion, and repeated reset suit Bob's kinetic-machine craft, but the Wish's decisive spectacle is projected silhouette geometry rather than an exposed linkage or gear train.

One obvious spin, compact support-free parts, broad load paths, and reset are good fits. Pico's three-part hard rule is unnecessarily restrictive here, and shadow projection is outside its primary craft.

Vela handles one-control transformations, indexed endpoints, rigid links, and tactile reset well, but Lantern Menagerie transforms a projected image rather than deploying the physical object's volume.
Ivy could make geometric optics physically legible and truthfully testable, but the Wish prioritizes theatrical creature magic over a science or mathematics teaching object.
The compact object and fold-out element overlap Mira's tactile transformation craft, but three shadow states and a wheel-driven optical mechanism are not a two-or-three-part pocket puzzle.
Negative space and flat-print silhouette vocabulary are relevant, yet the requested single assembled projection mechanism is not a modular mosaic or rearrangement toy.
A captive path could constrain wheel motion, but loops, crossings, and topology are not the source of the three optical transformations.
Eve's cinematic little-world instinct could enrich the moon-gate presence, but there is no personal real-world reference and the Wish is explicitly mechanism-first.
Passive geometry and hand power align only generally; playable sound is absent and acoustic geometry would distract from the shadow contract.
No tabletop rules, players, or simulation-driven game are requested.
No known tabletop classic or personal customization is requested.
No abstract strategy game, board structure, or combinatorial rules are requested.
